headline: Trump tells Israel who to pick. The vote is in eight days.
summary: Trump endorsed Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday after months of holding back; in June he called him "crazy." Israel votes October 27, its first election since October 7, 2023. Trump's post carried a warning: pick anyone but Netanyahu and America might not "finish the job" against Iran. The AP expects a tight race.
cover_answer: No. He gets an opinion. Israelis get the vote.
table_question: Should you tell a friend who to pick in their class vote?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: Israel is a country far away, and in eight days its grown-ups vote for their leader. On Sunday President Trump said he wants the leader they have now, Benjamin Netanyahu, to win again, like cheering for a friend who is running for class captain. Trump doesn't get a vote there. The people of Israel do.
5-7.why: Far away, a vote, a friend to cheer for. Who holds the vote is the one fact. At six, the vote they know is the classroom one, so that is the one in the script.
5-7.why_long: A six-year-old reasons from what is in front of them, so the script gives them a vote they have seen in class and a friend to cheer for, and it ends on who holds the ballot. The war with Iran can wait. Expect "does Trump get to vote there?" No. Only people who live in Israel do, and that is the whole answer.

8-12.script: Netanyahu wanted Trump's backing for months. They had fallen out over Iran; in June Trump called him "crazy." Sunday, nine days out, Trump endorsed him with a condition: pick anyone else and America might not help with Iran. A kid who lends his bike only if his friend is made captain.
8-12.why: Fell out, waited, endorsed, warned: a chain with a condition on the end. This age stops at the condition.
8-12.why_long: This age is checking whether adults keep their own rules, so the script runs the chain: a falling-out, months of silence, an endorsement nine days out, a condition on the end. The bike and the captain are a deal from their own playground. Expect "is that allowed?" Nothing stops it. Fair is theirs to call.

13-17.script: Endorsement or threat? Trump backed Netanyahu Sunday, then wrote that if Israel picks "the wrong Leader," America would face Iran alone. Second: this month he told Time "I'm not involved in politics anymore." He has endorsed in Hungary, Japan and Poland.
13-17.why: Two true things in one post, then his own words against his record. Teenagers test whether you will argue honestly, so hand them the quote.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things at once: Trump endorsed an ally, and he tied America's next move on Iran to how Israelis vote. The script asks which the post is, then sets his Time line against his record in Hungary, Japan and Poland. Expect "would we take this from another country?" Answer straight.

5-7.q: Does Trump get to vote in Israel?
5-7.a: No. Only people who live in Israel vote there. Trump just said who he is cheering for.

8-12.a: No. He posted who he wants to win. Only Israelis vote.

8-12.q: Why did he wait so long?
8-12.a: They fell out over the Iran war. In June he called him "crazy."

13-17.q: Was that an endorsement or a threat?
13-17.a: Both. Praise first, then America's next move on Iran tied to the result.

13-17.q: Would we want a foreign leader doing this to us?
13-17.a: Ask it back. He also endorsed in Hungary, Japan and Poland. Orbán lost.
